newsitem.title: UK: Europe crude outlook - Firmer on all fronts.
newsitem.headline: Europe crude outlook - Firmer on all fronts.

text.p: Delayed Nigerian loadings and dwindling early May North Sea supply should help push European crude markets higher this week, extending recent modest gains posted on the back of a recovery in refinery demand, traders said.
"There's demand from the U.S. and the Far East and I don't think they're finished buying yet," said a trader of Nigerian crude.
Nigerian and other West African crudes loading in May have flooded into the Asian market, attracted by margins which continue to offer the healthiest returns of all the main refining centres.

Crude has also been sailing transatlantic, helped by a widening Brent-WTI spread. Spot differentials should improve further this week after news late on Friday that Forcados cargoes loading May 7-20 would be delayed by three days due to ethnic clashes which forced Shell to shut in 90,000 barrels per day (bpd) of production.
"I expect we'll see the next Forcados trade at (Dated Brent) plus 10 cents," said a trader. The distillate-rich crude was talking around Dated Brent less five cents for much of last week.

The West African exodus to the East has also left gaps in the U.S. Gulf which North Sea producers have been only too happy to fill. Refiners there are running flat out to make up a stock shortfall in gasoline ahead of the peak summer driving season.

With the Brent-WTI spread standing at a robust $1.63 a barrel on Friday, traders expected more cargoes of Brent and other grades to follow recent heavy sailings, giving a further boost to spot market sentiment in northwest Europe.
"I think we'll see some continuity in the market. We're expecting to improve on last traded levels for a cargo we're showing," said a North Sea producer.
"There is plenty of demand and the first half of May is pretty well cleared out. Physically there's no reason for it to come down," said a trader for a major oil company.
Firm sentiment was reflected in the early keeping of all four Brent cargoes on Friday, traders said.
The cancellation of a Flotta cargo scheduled to load in May, which reduced the programme to 4.85 million barrels from the originally planned 5.45 million, gave the market another shot in the arm.
May loadings from the eight main North Sea systems should run about 60,000 bpd below April due to heavier maintenance.

Mediterranean sour crude markets were also expected to hold recently established higher levels, with good refining margins and delays at the Russian port of Novorossiisk more than compensating for rising Iraqi exports.

Iraqi Kirkuk, valued at 25 cents over its May sales price of Dated Brent -$2.20, continued to find plenty of buying interest. Rival Urals held steady with only one early May Urals cargoes on offer at around Dated Brent -$1.00.
Berth Two at Novorossiisk is expected to close on May 6 for about three weeks of scheduled repairs.
